results.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise
results.content:
## Introducing Firefox Enterprise

Firefox Enterprise is built for organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance requirements. It pairs the Firefox browser, built on Mozilla’s independent Gecko engine, with a management console organizations can run on their own infrastructure. From that console, IT teams can centrally manage browser policy and access, govern how data moves through the browser and set controls around AI use.

IT and security teams get more control over their data, IT infrastructure and browser environment — helping strengthen technological independence and operational resilience. [...] That means putting institutions in real control of the infrastructure and data they depend on, without asking them to rebuild or start over. Closing blind spots. Defining where policies, access and data live. Keeping core management within the institution’s environment. And bringing an overlooked layer — the browser — under institutional control.

Firefox Enterprise is unveiling across Europe with an initial sales focus on France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with more markets to follow. Thunderbird Enterprise is also in development, extending this customer-controlled approach to email and communications. We’ll have more to share as that work progresses.

If your organization wants greater control over its browser infrastructure, we’d like to work with you. [...] “If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, ‘choice’ is a lie. So is control,” said Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, CEO of Mozilla. “We built Firefox differently. And we’re bringing its independent architecture to institutions that are ready to rethink their dependencies and risk.”

## Bringing the browser under control

We’re starting with the browser because we see it as a key, but under-governed, layer. Firefox Enterprise gives institutions more control over the browser and the infrastructure managing it.

And because Firefox runs on Gecko, the only major browser engine developed outside Google and Apple, institutions have another path towards reducing dependence on a single architecture.

Firefox Enterprise’s key differentiation is its use of the Gecko browser engine, and its management console that can be deployed on a company’s own infrastructure, Levy said. This might make it a good fit for shops that want to minimize implementation disruptions to existing data management, access control, and compliance protocols.

“Firefox Enterprise lets customers craft their own deployment roadmap, assuming they have the skills and resources to self-manage the process,” Levy said.

BrowsersProductivity SoftwareEnterpriseBusinessMarketsIndustry

by  Taryn Plumb [...] The new offering combines the Firefox browser with a management console that enterprises can run on their own infrastructure using their own tooling. Companies get a full view of their data and can govern how it moves, and IT teams can manage policy, access, and set controls around AI use.

Firefox is already deployed across thousands of organizations and used by roughly 200 million people each month, Mozilla said. It is built on Mozilla’s independent Gecko engine, the only major browser engine developed outside Google and Apple.

“If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, ‘choice’ is a lie. So is control,” Mozilla CEO Anthony Enzor-DeMeo observed in the blog post announcing the product.

## The promise of Firefox Enterprise [...] Mozilla is particularly gearing Firefox Enterprise to organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance concerns. The offering can help enterprises meet regulatory requirements like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), the NIS2 directive, ISO27001, and SOC2.

IT teams can set external connection controls, allow or block organization-wide add-ons, and restrict browsing with a lockdown mode “so one zero-day doesn’t take down every browser in the estate,” the announcement said. AI use can be allowed, restricted, or disabled.

# Mozilla’s Firefox Enterprise lets companies block shadow AI in the browser

Mozilla’s Firefox Enterprise is a paid platform that lets organizations control how sensitive data is shared, check device security, and manage employee access to web applications.

The platform pairs the browser with a management dashboard hosted on an organization’s own infrastructure. IT teams can set policies across their workforce, restrict AI tools, and connect browser activity to existing security monitoring systems. [...] Mozilla is targeting organizations with demanding security and regulatory requirements.

### Controlling how sensitive data is shared

Firefox Enterprise lets administrators block or warn about pasting text, uploading files, downloading documents, and printing on selected websites. A company could prevent employees from pasting confidential material into an AI service it has not approved.

Built-in data protection checks run on the employee’s device. Organizations using a compatible third-party system can have that system handle the checks.

Data loss prevention (Source: Mozilla)

Administrators can allow, limit, or block AI services and disable browser AI features. Policies can apply to individual users or groups, allowing organizations to set different rules for different roles. [...] ### Bringing browser activity into security monitoring

Firefox Enterprise can export browser events and administrative actions to an organization’s security monitoring system. This gives security teams information they can use when investigating incidents and reviewing policy changes.

Security logging is optional, with administrators choosing the activities recorded and the level of detail. Records go to the organization’s dashboard. Employees see a notice explaining that their browser is managed.

Hosting the platform internally gives organizations control over management data, encryption keys, telemetry, and policies. Mozilla supplies the software, updates, and documentation, while customers operate the infrastructure and manage their data and governance requirements.
